notes: Petit taxis are metered (insist on it; 20–30 MAD), and the Careem app works. The medina is walkable. The airport taxi is a fixed 150 MAD; bus 19 costs 30 MAD.
October to April is ideal (20–25°C). Winter nights drop to 5°C and the Atlas is snowy (snow in Imlil). December and January are crowded; March and April bring orange blossom.

Stay in a riad (courtyard house) inside the medina; a porter for your luggage costs 20 MAD. The bargaining rule is a third of the first price. Offers of a 'guide' and the 'this road is closed' trick are scams.
Tagine 60–100 MAD, Jemaa stall meal 50, mint tea 15, Majorelle 170 (online), hammam 100–400; tip 10 MAD.
Women will be more comfortable with shoulders and knees covered. Mosque interiors are closed to non-Muslims (Koutoubia is seen from outside).
Turkish citizens can stay 90 days without a visa. Carry cash in MAD (from ATMs); cards work at riads and restaurants.

stops.name: Koutoubia Mosque
stops.tips: A 77 m minaret (twin of the Giralda in Seville). See it from outside and walk the gardens; it works as the medina's compass.

stops.name: Bahia Palace
stops.tips: A 19th-century vizier's palace with cedar ceilings and courtyards. It is quiet in the first hour.

stops.name: Saadian Tombs
stops.tips: 16th-century mausoleums rediscovered in 1917, with Carrara marble.

stops.name: Souks Marrakech
stops.tips: Labyrinthine markets selling leather (the Bab Debbagh tannery), lamps and carpets. Offer a third of the first price and turn down guide offers.

stops.name: Jemaa el-Fnaa at Night
stops.tips: A UNESCO-listed square with 100+ food stalls (harira, merguez, snails), storytellers and the Café de France terrace. Snake charmers will ask for money.

backups.name: Le Jardin Secret
backups.tips: A restored riad garden and tower: shade instead of the souks.

backups.name: Nomad Marrakech
backups.tips: Modern Moroccan food on a rooftop in Rahba Kedima. Book ahead.

stops.name: Jardin Majorelle
stops.tips: A cobalt-blue villa and cactus garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Buy tickets online for the 08:00 opening (they sell out); the Berber Museum is included.

stops.name: Musée Yves Saint Laurent
stops.tips: The museum next door. Combined ticket available, with a cafeteria.

stops.name: Gueliz Avenue Mohammed V
stops.tips: The French new town, with galleries and the 33 Rue Majorelle concept store.

stops.name: Grand Café de la Poste
stops.tips: A 1920s colonial brasserie in Gueliz.

stops.name: Menara Gardens
stops.tips: A 12th-century pool and pavilion. In winter you get views of the snowy Atlas peaks; come at sunset.

backups.name: Amal Women's Training Center
backups.tips: A restaurant run by a women's cooperative. Couscous on Fridays.

backups.name: Cyber Park Arsat Moulay Abdeslam
backups.tips: A shaded park beside the medina, a closer alternative to Menara.

stops.name: Imlil Village
stops.tips: 1.5 hours by taxi or tour (1,740 m). A Berber village at the foot of Toubkal, with mules and walnut trees.

stops.name: Aroumd Village Walk
stops.tips: A 1-hour climb from Imlil (guide 200 MAD). Terraced gardens and views of Toubkal, with snow in winter.

stops.name: Berber Home Lunch
stops.tips: Tagine and mint tea in a family home, on a terrace.

stops.name: Kasbah du Toubkal Terrace
stops.tips: Tea at a mountain kasbah with valley views. Proceeds support charity.

stops.name: Imlil Waterfall
stops.tips: A short walk above the village. Head back by 17:00.

backups.name: Ourika Valley Setti Fatma
backups.tips: An alternative valley: a 7-waterfall hike and riverside tagine. More touristy.

backups.name: Café Aksaoual Imlil
backups.tips: A café on the village square.

stops.name: Ben Youssef Madrasa
stops.tips: A 14th-century madrasa with zellij tilework and a cedar courtyard, 130 student cells, restored.

stops.name: Maison de la Photographie
stops.tips: Photographs of Morocco from 1870–1950. Coffee on the roof terrace with medina views.

stops.name: Le Jardin Marrakech
stops.tips: A restaurant in a green courtyard with tortoises, in Sidi Abdelaziz.

stops.name: Hammam de la Rose
stops.tips: A traditional hammam with black soap scrub mitt and argan massage. Separate hours for men and women.

stops.name: Terrasse des Épices
stops.tips: A rooftop restaurant with sunset views over the medina and tagine.

backups.name: Hammam Mouassine
backups.tips: A local public hammam: cheap, bring your own scrub mitt.

backups.name: Dar Cherifa
backups.tips: A 16th-century riad café-gallery with a literary focus.

stops.name: Skala de la Kasbah
stops.tips: 3 hours by Supratours bus (leaves Marrakech 07:00). Atlantic ramparts and cannons, a Game of Thrones filming location, and gulls.

stops.name: Essaouira Medina
stops.tips: A white-and-blue UNESCO medina with thuya wood workshops and art galleries.

stops.name: Essaouira Fishing Port
stops.tips: Fresh fish from the blue boats in the harbour, grilled at the stalls. Haggle by the kilo; try the sardines.

stops.name: Essaouira Beach
stops.tips: Winter wind and waves. Good for a walk along the shore.

stops.name: Taros Café
stops.tips: A rooftop terrace overlooking the harbour with gnawa music. Take the 17:30 bus back.

backups.name: Sidi Kaouki
backups.tips: A surf village beach 25 km away. Go by taxi.

stops.name: Mellah and Lazama Synagogue
stops.tips: The old Jewish quarter, with a spice market, the synagogue and the Miâara cemetery.

stops.name: Dar Si Said Museum
stops.tips: A museum of Moroccan carpets and woodwork, with the most beautiful courtyard.

stops.name: Marché Central Gueliz
stops.tips: The new town market: fruit and a quick lunch.

stops.name: Agafay Desert
stops.tips: A stony desert 40 minutes from the city. Camel rides, quad biking, sunset tea and camp dinner (tour about 400 MAD).

stops.name: Agafay Desert Camp Dinner
stops.tips: Tagine and Berber music at the camp, included in the tour. Stargazing.

backups.name: Palmeraie Camel Ride
backups.tips: A palm grove next to the city, a closer alternative to Agafay.

backups.name: Al Fassia Gueliz
backups.tips: Women-run Moroccan classics, including lamb shank.

days.theme: El Badi and a gentle farewell

stops.name: El Badi Palace
stops.tips: The ruins of a 16th-century 'incomparable' palace, with storks and pools, and the Koutoubia minbar.

stops.name: Place des Ferblantiers
stops.tips: The tinsmiths' square. Buy lamps as souvenirs and have a drink on the Kosybar terrace.

stops.name: Bacha Coffee Dar el Bacha
stops.tips: A coffee salon in a 1910 pasha's palace with 200 coffees. Expect a queue; a fitting farewell.

stops.name: Marrakech Menara Airport
stops.tips: 20 minutes by taxi (fixed 150 MAD). Farewell.

backups.name: Dar el Bacha Museum
backups.tips: A museum of cultural confluence, instead of the coffee.

backups.name: Patisserie des Princes
backups.tips: Moroccan sweets (kaab el ghzal), near Bab Agnaou.
